newsitem.title: UK: IRA suspect McAliskey has bail hearing adjourned.
newsitem.headline: IRA suspect McAliskey has bail hearing adjourned.

text.p: A pregnant Irish woman wanted in Germany for questioning about a 1996 bomb attack at a British army base will learn on Friday whether she has been granted bail, her lawyers said on Tuesday.

Lawyers for Roisin McAliskey, who argued at a private High Court hearing that she should be released from London's Holloway prison on health grounds, said the judge had adjourned the case until Friday.

McAliskey, 25, has been in Holloway since last November while Germany seeks her extradition on charges of being involved in an Irish Republican Army (IRA) mortar attack on a British army barracks in Osnabrueck last year.
McAliskey, due to give birth in May, denies the charge.
Last Friday British authorities eased her prison conditions by downgrading her security classification and saying she would not be subjected to frequent strip searches.
Her supporters say she has been subjected to "barbaric and inhumane conditions" in prison, but the Prison Service says her treatment has been "appropriate and humane".

The IRA called a ceasefire in its battle to oust Britain from Northern Ireland in August 1994. The truce was broken 17 months later with a series of attacks on targets in mainland Britain before the Osnabrueck attack.
Britain decided to detain McAliskey -- daughter of veteran Irish nationalist campaigner Bernadette McAliskey, nee Devlin -- because it was felt she was likely to abscond.
